package_info.package_versions: Unknown (latest version at time of campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The FlixOnline app is a malicious Android application that masquerades as a legitimate Netflix content enabler. It abuses Android permissions to intercept WhatsApp messages, spread itself via WhatsApp conversations, and distribute further malicious payloads, exhibiting classic worm and spyware behaviors.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation and user grants permissions)
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (Android APK, likely MainActivity.java or a background service)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The app requests permissions to overlay on top of other apps, read and send SMS, and access WhatsApp notifications. It monitors incoming WhatsApp messages and automatically replies to them with a malicious link to download the FlixOnline APK.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code monitors WhatsApp notifications, intercepts incoming messages, and automatically replies with a malicious download link, enabling self-propagation and further payload distribution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and replying to WhatsApp messages without user interaction is a clear sign of malicious intent, especially when the reply contains a link to a malicious APK.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps do not monitor or auto-reply to WhatsApp messages, nor do they propagate themselves via messaging platforms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some accessibility or automation apps may interact with notifications, but not for self-propagation or malware distribution.
key_indicators: Abuse of notification listener to access WhatsApp messages

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation and user grants permissions)
execution_context.file_location: Background service or broadcast receiver within the APK

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The app exfiltrates the user's contact list and SMS messages to a remote command and control server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads the user's contact list and SMS messages, then sends this data to a remote server controlled by the attacker, enabling data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating personal data such as contacts and SMS messages to an external server is a hallmark of spyware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not send sensitive user data to unknown remote servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup apps may upload contacts/SMS to cloud storage, but with clear user consent and reputable endpoints.
key_indicators: Network communication to unknown C2 server
Access to sensitive user data (contacts, SMS)
No legitimate user-facing reason for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User installs the FlixOnline app from Google Play, believing it to be a Netflix content enabler.
attack_chain.leads_to: App requests excessive permissions and begins background activity.

attack_chain.action: App requests overlay, SMS, contacts, and notification access permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: App gains ability to monitor WhatsApp and access sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: App monitors WhatsApp notifications and automatically replies to incoming messages with a malicious APK download link.
attack_chain.leads_to: Propagation to new victims via WhatsApp.

attack_chain.action: App reads user's contacts and SMS messages, exfiltrating them to a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive user data.

attack_chain.action: App may download and execute further malicious payloads as instructed by the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further compromise of the device or network.

behavioral_signatures: Android app requesting overlay, SMS, contacts, and notification access permissions without clear justification
Automatic replies to WhatsApp messages containing APK download links
Exfiltration of contacts and SMS data to external servers
file_indicators: Presence of code accessing NotificationListenerService for WhatsApp
Unusual background services with network activity
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious C2 domains/IPs
Frequent HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing contact/SMS data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request excessive permissions (overlay, SMS, contacts, notification access) and observe for automatic WhatsApp replies containing APK links. Analyze network traffic for exfiltration of contacts/SMS data to unknown servers. Use mobile security solutions to flag apps with notification listener abuse and self-propagation behaviors.
